rules.title: Do not silently discard Result errors (let _ =, if let Ok, .ok(), .ok().flatten())
rules.problem: Reviewers repeatedly catch fallible calls whose errors are dropped: `let _ = client.sync()`, `if let Ok(x) = conn.query_row_and_then_cachable(..)`, `store.cleanup_expired().ok()`, `filter_map(|r| r.ok().flatten())` over query_map rows, `if let Ok(Some(..))`. Real DB/network/serde failures then vanish or get mistaken for 'no rows', making bugs undiagnosable.
rules.rule: In non-test code under components/, a Result must be propagated with `?`, matched explicitly, or logged (`warn!`/`error!`/report_error!) before being discarded. Banned forms: `let _ = <expr returning Result>`, `<expr>.ok();` as a statement, `if let Ok(..) = <sql query>` used to mean 'row exists' (use `try_query_one`/`try_query_row` + `?`), and `.ok()`/`.ok().flatten()` inside `filter_map` over rusqlite `query_map` rows (collect into `Result<Vec<_>>` instead).
rules.detect: [workspace.lints.clippy] let_underscore_must_use = "warn", unused_result_ok = "warn" (both restriction). Plus ast-grep rules: (1) `if let Ok($P) = $C.$Q($$$)` where $Q matches /query_row|query_one|query_row_and_then/; (2) `$IT.filter_map(|$x| $x.ok()$$$)` and `.ok().flatten()` when receiver comes from `query_map`/`query_and_then`; (3) `if let Ok(Some($P)) = $E` -> suggest `match`/`?`. Allow-list via `// error intentionally ignored: <reason>` comment on the preceding line.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - some fallbacks are intentional (e.g. cache lookup falling back to network); require an explanatory comment or explicit log to silence
